purpose: Generated illustrative enterprise hardware scene; not a photograph of actual InterData infrastructure.
prompt:
Use case: product-mockup.
Asset type: new website hero background for an enterprise VPS AMD service page, ultra-wide landscape approximately 2.4:1.
Primary request: a highly realistic, understated enterprise technology photograph featuring an AMD EPYC processor physically installed in a server motherboard in the right foreground, with actual-looking data-center server racks softly out of focus behind it. The chip, motherboard and room must be one coherent photographic scene. This should look like professional hardware product photography, with natural physical materials and believable scale.
Composition: the left 46% is clean dark navy negative space with very subtle blurred rack detail for an HTML headline, paragraph and two buttons. The installed processor is centered around 74% across the frame and around 52% of the height, occupying approximately 18–22% of image width; its entire top and socket must be visible with comfortable space around it. Use a close three-quarter view into an opened rackmount server chassis on a maintenance bench. A compact brushed-silver processor with crisp black "AMD EPYC" label is seated flat in a realistic dark gray motherboard socket. Background racks recede naturally at much larger physical scale, out of focus. This is a close camera view of normal-sized hardware, not a giant chip in a server aisle.
Style: sophisticated commercial photography, restrained, practical, premium B2B infrastructure, realistic 50mm camera perspective, gently shallow depth of field, believable circuit-board detail, matte metal chassis, controlled highlights, fine material texture.
Lighting and palette: soft neutral white key light on the silver processor, subdued navy / slate / charcoal environment, tiny ordinary blue server status LEDs only. Dark areas retain gentle detail. No saturated cyan light trails, no RGB gaming lighting, no luminous circuit traces, no bloom, no holograms, no futuristic pedestal, no particles, no science-fiction props, no floating chip, no excessive blue color cast on metal.
Text: only the authentic-looking black chip marking "AMD EPYC"; no other legible text, no website interface, no buttons, no watermark, no certification, no extra logos. Opaque edge-to-edge background.
